sports.name: Baseball
sports.tag: Find your place on the diamond.
sports.summary: From a first swing to competitive league play. A pathway for every stage of development.
programs: T-Ball

An introduction to hitting and fielding with a batting tee and on-field coaching. The published program meets one or two days per week at Cetronia Elementary. Bring a glove; league bats are available.
Coach Pitch
Coach-pitched batting and supportive instruction. The published program lists three days per week at Lone Lane Park. Bring a glove; league bats are available.
Grasshopper
A transition toward player pitching, with coaches supporting play under league rules. Published sessions take place three days per week at Parkway Manor Elementary. A glove and bat are required.
League pathways
Parkland Youth League offers developmental and competitive divisions. Lehigh Valley League, Connie Mack and Senior Legion have specific selection and eligibility requirements.
sports.note: Introductory age cutoffs in the source still refer to 2025. Confirm the current division, schedule and equipment list before enrolling.

sports.name: Basketball
sports.tag: More than a game. A team.
sports.summary: Build confidence on the court through recreational and competitive opportunities.
programs: Summer recreation
The published 2026 program served children entering grades 3–12, with practices and games at Grange Park. It emphasized games rather than intensive practice.
Winter basketball
The association overview describes winter recreational and travel opportunities. Ask the commissioner for the upcoming season's grades, evaluations and schedule.
sports.note: The summer registration dates have passed. Upcoming winter dates and fees require confirmation.

sports.name: Cheer
sports.tag: Bring the energy. Share the spirit.
sports.summary: Find friendship, confidence and team spirit through cheerleading.
programs: Flags & Junior Pee Wee
The 2026 listing places Kindergarten in Flags and first grade in Junior Pee Wee.
Pee Wee & Junior Varsity
Second and third grades are listed under Pee Wee; fourth and fifth under Junior Varsity.
Varsity
The published Varsity group covers sixth through eighth grades. Divisions may change depending on participation.
sports.note: Confirm availability, practice times, fees and the equipment provided with the cheer commissioners.

sports.name: Field Hockey
sports.summary: Recreational field hockey built around learning, balanced teams and friendship.
sports.commitment: Spring: one or two sessions weekly
programs: Fall field hockey
Players undergo an evaluation to help form evenly skilled teams. The evaluation supports team balance; it is not a selection tryout.
Spring skills & drills
A skills-only season without games. Published groups range from Kindergarten through seventh grade, with one or two practices per week depending on grade.
sports.note: The source references July 2026 evaluation updates. Contact the commissioner for current dates and placement.

sports.name: Football
sports.summary: A division-based football program that develops skills, sportsmanship and teamwork.
sports.audience: Age and weight eligibility by division
programs: Football flag program
An introductory flag division within the football program. This is separate from SPYA's NFL Flag program.
Junior Pee Wee & Pee Wee
Age and weight rules apply to each division. The 2026 source includes changed cutoffs and a special returning-player provision.
Junior Varsity & Varsity
Competitive divisions with specific age and weight limits. Review the full official rules with the commissioner before selecting a division.
sports.note: Do not choose a division from age alone. Confirm current age, weight and returning-player rules before registration.

sports.name: Lacrosse
sports.tag: Pick up a stick. Find your team.
sports.summary: An introduction to the sport and a pathway through boys' and girls' team programs.
programs: Mini-Scoopers
A playful introduction listed for ages 3–5. The source describes a weekly seven-week program with sticks and soft balls supplied.
Boys' & girls' teams
Published grade groups are K–2, 3–4, 5–6 and 7–8. Team structure and competitive brackets vary.
Equipment & uniforms
Loaner equipment is described as first come, first served, with refundable deposits for boys and girls. Uniforms may require a separate purchase.
Volunteering
The published program includes a reimbursable family volunteer fee. Ask about eligible roles, hours and the reimbursement process.
sports.note: The source mixes a 2026 season announcement with a 2024 Mini-Scoopers deadline. Confirm all upcoming dates, charges and equipment availability.

sports.name: NFL Flag
sports.summary: Recreational 5v5 flag football with multiple seasons and age-group divisions.
programs: 5v5 recreation
A community-focused program for a range of skill levels, with five age-group divisions.
Seasonal play
The source lists fall, winter and spring seasons, plus a skills program between fall and winter.
Choose the correct program
NFL Flag is separate from the flag division offered by SPYA Football. Age cutoff dates vary by season.
sports.note: As of the September 15, 2026 source review, fall registration was marked closed. Confirm the next registration window with the commissioner.

sports.name: Soccer
sports.summary: In-house, recreational and travel pathways, with opportunities to build skills.
sports.commitment: Travel described as a two-season commitment
programs: In-house & recreation
Explore the official registration information for available divisions and age groups.
Travel soccer
The association overview describes a two-season commitment with tryouts. Confirm current arrangements and selection dates.
Summer skills & scrimmages
The published summer sessions combined skill training with small-sided scrimmages. Contact SPYA about future sessions.
sports.note: The source lists the commissioner position as open. Use the soccer contact or board directory for current program questions.

sports.name: Softball
sports.summary: Youth softball with a local home field and opportunities across age divisions.
programs: Youth divisions
The source lists regular 8u, 10u and 12u teams, with a 14u team possible when interest permits.
Home field
Practices and home games are listed at Springhouse Middle School, 1200 Springhouse Road, Allentown.
Late registration
Families are asked to contact the commissioner after the registration window closes; a place depends on available capacity.
sports.note: The page's August 1 registration deadline has passed relative to the source review. Confirm availability directly.
